title: onprem/airgap: vendor offline bundle + add Rancher / Flatcar support for private-installer
author: Jordan Li
description:
Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in air-gapped/on-prem environments have a variety of host OS and distro packaging constraints (Rancher-managed clusters, Flatcar/Container Linux, etc.). This PR updates the private-installer offline bundle tooling to vendor required OS packages and container images, adds explicit support for Rancher-provisioned clusters and Flatcar/Container Linux nodes, and includes Helm chart tweaks and Terraform module updates needed for reproducible offline installs and safe rollbacks.

What this changes (high level):
- bundle-builder: vendor additional runtime packages (containerd systemd unit fragments, crictl, runc/containerd-shim compat files) into the offline bundle and add metadata for distro-specific installation hooks.
- installer helm charts: add tolerations, nodeSelector options, and systemd unit template overlays to handle Flatcar's readonly /usr and ephemeral mounts.
- private-installer: add a Rancher detection codepath and mapping that applies the correct CNI/container runtime preflight steps when the cluster is managed by Rancher.
- terraform/redwood-private: expose new variables for local_registry mirror endpoint and skip_tls_verify toggles (used in air-gapped mirrors).
- upgrade/rollback tooling: extend preflight/rollback hooks to validate bundle manifest checksums, preserve previous helm release values in a rollback snapshot, and test-apply a dry-run of the migration steps.

Checklist included in PR description: 
- [x] vendor container images and tarballs for amd64/arm64 where applicable
- [x] include distro-specific install hooks for Flatcar and RHEL/CentOS variants
- [x] Helm chart changes with minimal behavioral impact for default users
- [x] Terraform module bump and migration notes
- [x] e2e airgap lab run (see CI checks below)

Testing and verification: ran airgap E2E in the benchmark-lab using a Rancher-provisioned k8s cluster with Flatcar nodes. Verified: 1) installer can bootstrap using offline bundle and local registry mirror, 2) helm charts render correctly with the new overlays, 3) rollback snapshot restores previous release values and service endpoints, 4) smoke tests for inference API return 200 in hosted-local mode.

Notes / migration guidance: offline bundle must be re-generated and shipped to customers using the bundle-builder release; customers using the terraform module should set local_registry and mirror_ca_bundle when deploying into air-gapped networks. The new flags are backward compatible: default path keeps previous behavior.

References: related PRs in repo: pr-20482 (previous bundle work), pr-21457 (kube distro compat). Linked Linear tickets ENG-2310, ENG-2387 for rollout and post-merge follow-ups.

discussion: Priya Nair: Can we avoid adding distro-specific logic in the installer runtime? Suggest pushing mapping to bundle metadata and keep runtime generic.

Jordan Li (author): Agreed — moved the mapping into the bundle manifest and added a lightweight detector in runtime that only reads the manifest. Kept Rancher detection minimal to avoid heavy k8s API calls.
Marcus Chen: Helm changes look fine, but please ensure values.yaml defaults preserve existing behavior. Also request that systemd overlays are opt-in behind a feature flag.
Jordan Li (author): Added 'enableSystemdOverlay' flag (default: false) and documented it in onprem-airgap.md. Updated tests to exercise both code paths.
Elena Garcia: CI flake on the e2e airgap test (timeout) — re-ran job after bumping probe timeouts. All green now.
Priya Nair: Approving — verified rollback snapshot behavior in local lab. Marcus: Approved. Merged by squash-merge after CI green.

release_notes: Added Rancher and Flatcar compatibility for private-installer offline bundles. Bundles now vendor required runtime binaries and include distro-specific install hooks. New terraform variables: local_registry, mirror_ca_bundle. Opt-in systemd overlay for Flatcar. No breaking changes by default; customers in air-gapped environments should regenerate offline bundles and supply local registry endpoints.
